Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the mini conference of Block 2. My name is Sofia, and I am your moderator today. Our panel has three speakers, and each one has a time slot of three minutes. After the three talks, we will have fifteen minutes for questions. Our topic this afternoon is trust in football: how clubs, sponsors and federations build it, and how they lose it. Our first panelist works in sports marketing in Madrid. Our second panelist is Doctor Nilo Patussi, chief compliance officer at a major Brazilian club. And our third panelist is a sports journalist from Mexico City. Please keep your phones on silent, and write down your questions as you listen. What I want you to remember is that there are no bad questions today. So, let's start.

Thank you, Sofia. My key message today is simple: trust is a contract that nobody signs. Let me give you one case. Two years ago, my club was negotiating a renewal with a big sponsor. The sponsor said that they wanted a longer contract, and we wanted a higher fee. We found a compromise, and the vote was unanimous. But what really closed the deal was not the money. It was our track record. The sponsor told us that they had checked every audit from the last five years. The reason why they trusted us is that we had always published the results, the good ones and the bad ones. So my takeaway for you is this: if you want partners to trust you tomorrow, be transparent today. Thank you.
